A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PERM and contain 27 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. The corresponding equations, three tables, and 35 figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction experiments, architecture ablations, and synthesis and editing results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including reconstruction errors in Tables 1–3 and qualitative application results.

M1.justification: The frequency-domain PCA representation, StyleGAN2 guide generator, U-Net upsampler, residual VAE, losses, and reconstruction procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use augmented USC-HairSalon, the same 17 test hairstyles, and the private dataset of 80 groomed hairstyles. Reconstruction, interpolation, dynamic-hair, and image-generation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same strand VAE/PCA alternatives, GroomGen, HairStep, HAAR, architecture ablations, and interpolation/video baselines. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training and test counts, preprocessing, strand resolution, latent dimensions, error metrics, and training/fitting schedules are unchanged. The relocated private-dataset paragraph describes an experiment already present in v4.

E4.justification: Appendices B.4 and C retain the same PCA-component sensitivity studies, private-dataset checks, architecture ablations, and GroomGen verification. The qualitative robustness and failure examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, plotted trends, and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Section 4.2 retains PERM's position/curvature errors of 1.658/0.769 and GroomGen's 2.570/6.199.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 retain their substance. Changing the vector Gaussian notation from N(0, 1) to N(0, I) in Section 3.2.1 clarifies the existing distribution rather than introducing a different assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: disentangled global structure and local curls, a compact parametric hair representation, and reuse across reconstruction, editing, and conditional generation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of reconstruction quality and architecture behavior are retained. Appendix E preserves the limitations concerning underrepresented hairstyles, unnatural samples, and failures of image-based reconstruction.

D1.justification: Appendix B.5 changes the fitted parametric hair dataset from one the authors 'will release' to one they 'released as well.' This updates reported resource availability; implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and training times remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Prior-work coverage and novelty positioning are retained. Section 2 now explicitly describes GroomGen's deterministic upsampling, already described in v4 Section 3.2.2. The Herrera simulator reference receives a title and bibliographic update rather than introducing another work.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited grammatical edits, consolidates and moves paragraphs, and updates acknowledgments and reference metadata. Appendix B.4 corrects a reference from Figure 18 to Figure 14; the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the ICLR 2025 page header and modestly reflows the document. Figure 1's caption clarifies wisps, Table 3's caption refers to guide textures, and some labels are standardized; all figure panels and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves clarity through copyediting, clearer notation and captions, and the corrected Figure 14 cross-reference. Appendix B.5 also updates the dataset's reported release status. These improve presentation and resource documentation, while the scientific evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
